THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 7 were held and are listed below with their citations; 41 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, core_pcr, comp_risc_superscalar, comp_relational_database, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_geostationary_comsat, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_composite_structures, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_recombinant_pharma, bio_universal_immunisation, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_cross_sectional_imaging, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_electronic_freight_documents, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. core_packet_internetworking -> HELD (semiconductors-computing said not held, telecom-space said held; resolved to the board that owns the Communications domain, telecom-space).

granted.source: Route (a) production. Samsung Electronics developed the 4-Mbit DRAM - the 0.8-micron generation - in February 1988 at the Giheung fab (Line 1, opened 1984), was making 4-Mbit chips by 1989, and developed its 16-Mbit part in September 1990. Corroboration for use: IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 3.72 PCs per 100. CONFIDENCE: the February 1988 development date and the September 1990 16-Mbit date are firm across sources; the 1989 production start is reported in the Samsung technological-capability literature (BRIE/UC Berkeley working paper 106, 'Technological Capabilities and Samsung Electronics') which I could not read in full this session.

SDN (System Development Network) began operating on 15 May 1982, linking Seoul National University to the Korea Institute of Electronics Technology over TCP/IP at 1200 bps - a domestically built and domestically administered TCP/IP network, generally described as the second such network in the world after ARPANET and the first outside the US and Europe. It grew into the national research and education network and its international links were initially UUCP, so the IP routing and hosts were Korea's own. Kilnam Chon's SDN is documented in 'A Brief History of the Internet in Korea' and in his Internet Hall of Fame citation.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 3.72 PCs per 100, 1.5x the World value of 2.45. Corroboration: Samsung, Hyundai and Goldstar were all producing DRAM and PC hardware domestically by 1989.

TDX-1, Korea's indigenous digital electronic switching system developed by ETRI, was opened to certification traffic on 25 April 1984 and entered commercial service on 14 March 1986 at Songjeong-ri, Gyeonggi-do, with 362 subscribers. R3 confirms: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 80,005 Korean mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 80,005 Korean mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990, a stock incompatible with a 1990 launch; Korea's car-telephone cellular service had been operating since the mid-1980s and the network's mobile switching centres are the same TDX-family infrastructure ETRI commercialised from 14 March 1986.
Samsung developed its 4 Mb DRAM in 1988 and carried it into production at Giheung; Hyundai and Goldstar were also in DRAM production by the end of the decade.

The 'White Revolution' (baeksaek hyeongmyeong) is the standard Korean name for the spread of plastic-film greenhouses, plastic mulch and polytunnels through the 1980s and 1990s, which turned the colour of the Korean agricultural landscape from green to white; the ministry's hi-tech greenhouse subsidy programme follows in the 1990s. LIMIT STATED: the phenomenon is named and dated to the 1980s-90s, so at 1 Jan 1990 it was in mid-course rather than complete.
